what_it_does: As conventional transistor scaling reaches its limits, superconducting electronics offer an alternative path for ultra-low-power and high-speed computation. This paper builds the first full-system simulator for a hybrid architecture combining superconducting CPU cores (running at 100 billion cycles per second) with cryogenic semiconductor cores (4 billion cycles per second), plus multi-level caches and a superconducting interconnection network connecting specialized hardware accelerators. Tests on scientific computing benchmarks reveal the bottlenecks and design tradeoffs unique to this technology.
